children: shares reached a new 52-week high on Thursday after an FDA advisory panel voted in favor of the company’s multi-cancer early detection test, Galleri, setting up a potential approval for the blood-based screening test in the U.S.

In three separate votes late Wednesday, the Molecular and Clinical Genetics Devices Panel of the Medical Devices Advisory Committee endorsed a premarket approval for Galleri, which is currently under FDA review with a decision

While FDA advisory panels issue non-binding recommendations that the regulator typically follows, Wall Street analysts were bullish on a potential premarket nod for Galleri, which can screen for over 50 types of cancer.

RBC Capital Markets analyst Dan Leonard, who has a Sector Perform rating on Grail (GRAIL), argued that the vote is an “obvious positive” and boosts the prospects for a possible FDA nod for Galleri before the year-end.
Leonard called “Galleri’s progress a tailwind for the entire multi-cancer detection
category” and said that, however, the market has “missed the mark” in selling off Guardant Health
, another player in early cancer detection.
Canaccord Genuity analyst Kyle Mikson, who has a Buy rating on GRAIL
, said that he remains “bullish on GRAL shares," as the AdCom meeting "went generally better than we expected.”

“Speakers emphasized that the test should be viewed as a complementary tool to existing recommended screening methods,” Bloomberg reported, quoting Mikson. He added that even without an “early” detection label, Galleri remains appealing.

However, BTIG analyst Mark Massaro noted that the panelists' votes on the effectiveness and the benefit/risk profile of the test were “closer than we expected.” “We think today’s panel should most likely (but is not a lock to) bode well for the company’s FDA approval prospects, and importantly, we think a rising tide is likely to lift many boats,” Massaro wrote.
The analyst cites positive read-through to other MCED test developers, including Guardant Health

title: GRAIL sets new 52-week high as FDA panel backs cancer test
